subject: Dedicated GPU pool capacity throttle — HeliosAI update and action plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@heliosai.com>
Cc: HeliosAI Platform Team <platform@heliosai.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed errors & latency — immediate acknowledgement

Sara —

Thanks for flagging this. We’re actively investigating the elevated 504s and latency you reported for jobs running against your Dedicated GPU pool in eu-west-1. Immediate summary:

- Impact window (prelim): 2026-04-15T14:05:00Z — 2026-04-15T17:08:00Z (approx 3h).
- Visible symptoms: increased tail latency for long-running batches, intermittent 502/504, queuing of scheduled runs.
- Customer-visible: HeliosAI production inference jobs experienced degraded throughput and some failed requests.

Preliminary findings (work in progress): we observed an automated capacity throttle triggered by a thermal imbalance on a subset of GPU hosts. The serving scheduler reduced available GPU slots to protect hardware, which caused persistent backpressure. At the same time the autoscaler attempted to provision replacement instances but was blocked by an internal quota check race (INFRA-4721) leading to delayed scale-up.

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Manually disabled the faulty thermal-trigger policy for the affected pool and rebalanced workloads (completed).
- Escalated quota race fix to infra on-call and pushed a hotfix to the autoscaler (in progress).
- Opened JIRA INFRA-4721; attached a high-level timeline (incident_timeline.pdf).

We’ll provide a full timeline and remediation plan in the next 2–4 hours. I’m committing a temporary capacity bump to HeliosAI’s dedicated pool while we complete the autoscaler fix — this should restore normal throughput. Apologies for the disruption; we know this impacts running tasks and schedules.

If you can share a short list of the highest-priority jobs that were impacted, we’ll queue them for expedited rerun once capacity is stable.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai
[attachment: incident_timeline.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@heliosai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 09:10:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Observed errors & latency — immediate acknowledgement

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the quick note. A couple of asks from our side:

- Can you quantify how many requests and what % of throughput were affected?
- ETA on the autoscaler hotfix and the timeline for the temporary capacity bump to be fully in effect?
- Are there any data integrity concerns we should be worried about for the failed/queued jobs?

We had a handful of nightly batch runs fail (IDs: job_1292, job_1294) and one customer-facing stream that showed retries. Please prioritize job_1292 and job_1294.

Sara Bloom
Director, Platform Engineering — HeliosAI
sara.bloom@heliosai.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 09:20:45 -0700
Subject: HeliosAI incident — immediate coordination

Laura / Monica —

Looping you in to coordinate the customer comms and remediation. Summary: thermal-triggered capacity throttle hit HeliosAI dedicated pool in eu-west-1; autoscaler race prevented timely scale-up. Customer impact includes failed batch jobs and elevated latencies; they asked for priority reruns.

Immediate asks:
- Monica: please validate the manual capacity bump completed and confirm exact increase in available GPU slots (PRIV-> report back).
- Laura: can we pre-authorize a one-off credit for HeliosAI while we finalize root cause? Recommend 10% of April bill as a gesture; I’ll loop legal if needed.
- Rachel: please start drafting a concise external-facing timeline we can share; include the mitigation steps and next actions.

Attached a diff with the quick mitigation we plan to push to the autoscaler to remove the quota check race (mitigation_patch.diff). Infra on-call says the patch is low-risk but needs a rolling restart. I’ll coordinate the deploy with ops.

Tentative timeline: hotfix deploy by 11:00 UTC, validate by 12:00 UTC; if green, schedule reruns for impacted jobs by 13:00 UTC.

Thanks — I’ll update Sara as soon as we validate.

Marcus
Account Executive

[attachment: mitigation_patch.diff (text)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@heliosai.com>
Cc: HeliosAI Platform Team <platform@heliosai.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 13:45:03 +0000
Subject: Update: capacity bump applied and autoscaler fix deployed

Sara —

Quick update following the earlier note:

- We deployed the autoscaler hotfix (INFRA-4721) at 10:50 UTC and performed a rolling restart; the quota race is resolved.
- We applied a manual +20% capacity bump to HeliosAI’s dedicated pool in eu-west-1 at 11:10 UTC; we validated increased slot availability at 11:25 UTC.
- Validation: over the 11:30–13:00 UTC window, average throughput returned to normal and failed-request rate dropped to baseline.

We’ve prioritized job_1292 and job_1294 for rerun; both completed successfully at 12:40 UTC. No evidence of data corruption for retried jobs — retries were idempotent and completed without errors.

Next steps:
- Final postmortem with timeline and permanent fixes will be delivered by EOD tomorrow.
- We intend to ship a permanent protection change to the thermal-triggering policy and add a guardrail in autoscaler to prevent the quota race.
- As pre-authorized by Laura, we will apply a one-off account credit; I’ll confirm amounts once finance completes the calc.

Apologies again for the interruption. I can set up a 30-minute bridge if you want to walk through the timeline and planned fixes with engineering.

Best,
Marcus
marcus@redwood.ai

[attachment: incident_timeline.pdf (pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bloom <sara.bloom@heliosai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Final postmortem — HeliosAI dedicated pool throttle (April 15, 2026)

Sara / Helios team —

Thank you for your patience while we completed our investigation. Attached is the final postmortem draft (final_postmortem_draft.md) and the timeline PDF. Below is an executive summary and the concrete action items.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: a thermal protection policy misclassification on a subset of GPU hosts caused the serving scheduler to temporarily withdraw capacity from HeliosAI’s dedicated pool. Concurrently, an autoscaler quota validation race (INFRA-4721) blocked scale-up attempts. The combination led to sustained backpressure and elevated failed requests.
- Impact: approximately 3 hours of degraded throughput (2026-04-15T14:05Z–17:08Z). Affected HeliosAI production jobs (est. 4.3% of daily requests during the window). Two scheduled batch jobs failed and were retried successfully.
- Customer remediation: manual capacity bump (+20%) applied; autoscaler hotfix deployed; impacted jobs rerun and validated. No data integrity issues found.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- INFRA-4721: implement autoscaler guardrail to prevent quota race — Owner: infra on-call (monica_patel) — Due: 2026-05-01
- Thermal policy review: audit and tighten host classification thresholds — Owner: ops (rachel_kim) — Due: 2026-04-22
- Monitoring: add a synthetic test and alert for sudden slot withdrawals in dedicated pools — Owner: observability (leads) — Due: 2026-04-30
- Billing gesture: apply 10% credit for April usage — Owner: finance (laura_bennett) — Due: 2026-04-19

We regret the disruption and will share an updated runbook describing the emergency workflow for dedicated pools. If you’d like, we can schedule a short review next week to walk through the postmortem and the changes we’ll make.

Sincerely,
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
